bifurcation.note: W1-04 is judged on the Morrowind side. The pictures in this verdict are cited as fidelity evidence for structural claims - roofs covering their footprints, a doorstep inside its own building, a town with no street surface - and not as art-direction judgements. The Souls-side crossings the piece carries are reported under AR-3.

sim/npc.js#anchorFor() derives interior anchors from d.bounds_m and applyInteriorBounds() mutates the same record objects, so a room that shrank shrank for the people in it; the 1.2 m inset never exceeds a half-extent (smallest joined room 4.34 x 10.94 m, 0 of 115 collapse). That is the builder's 'by reference' claim verified. Three people still stand in masonry outdoors.

REGRESSED by the join. 55 authored lamps in 19 of the 41 shrunk rooms now stand outside their own room's bounds - 12 of them non-snuffable hearths, worst 2.33 m outside - and 0 in any room the join did not shrink, so the join caused every one. render/interior.js places lamps at L.pos verbatim and sim/stealth/system.js#syncInteriorLights() adds a detection light source at the identical verbatim pos on the fixed step, so the lights the Souls-side detection model reads are outside the rooms they light. applyInteriorBounds() already clamps continuity.interior_spawn for exactly this reason and does not clamp lights[]. ar3.note: Two crossings now, not one. Round 3's stands: the town's masonry becomes sim.cell and sim/stealth/system.js:223 reads sim.cell.shapes.length to decide whether cover exists at all, so a town's buildings decide whether you can be seen in its street. Round 4 adds a second: applyInteriorBounds() now sizes the rooms whose authored lamps sim/stealth/system.js#syncInteriorLights() feeds into the Souls-side detection curve on the fixed step, so a settlement-layout decision propagates into detection. That second crossing carries a defect - the lamps were not clamped with the room - which is reported as a blocking gap. A seam that carries a bug is a seam that carries something. inCoverFraction on both arms is STILL not measured, for a third round.

score.note: Round 1 3.2 (gate 6), round 2 4.4, round 3 4.6, now 4.7. The round closed the blocking gap it was given, and I verified the closure with instruments the builder did not write. what_the_round_got_right: The distinctness measure survives every degenerate case I could invent. Empty scene = 0 meshes and the hash of nothing; the same room at 0/2/60/600 fixed steps = ONE hash where the pixel sweep returned 8 of 8 distinct after 2 steps; two camera poses = 1; a mesh removed, a 1 cm move and a non-numeric name change all change it; the positive control separates street, room and other room 3 of 3. Two acceptance numbers in this piece were proved unmeasurable in consecutive rounds; this one is not.

The roofs are fixed, verified with an independent 8x8 raycast (0 of 202 fail, worst coverage 1.000) whose red arm I demonstrated (201 of 202 fail when roof meshes are scaled 0.7 in plan). The builder's note that a bounding box could not see the defect and a raycast could is right and generalises.
The join reproduces independently: 41 of 112 before, 0 after, worst area ratio 1.0887, 41 rooms limited, worst archon-market keeping 17.1%.

'By reference' is a real claim and it is true: applyInteriorBounds() mutates the record objects sim/npc.js#anchorFor() reads, so a room that shrank shrank for the people in it, and the 1.2 m anchor inset never exceeds a half-extent.
The api.js nulling pattern one verb below the round-3 fix is gone, with the voided measurement named in the comment.
The three prop builders that threw are fixed and the silent fallback accounting with them.
VP04 is out of thorn-sapwell and photographs a legible town.

biggest_gap.what: buildings[].door is the building's own centre on 112 of 112 (max door-to-centre distance 0.00 m), and every declared continuity.exterior_spawn lies inside its own building's wall box - settlementSolids() centres the four wall slabs on b.x,b.z with half-extents w/2,d/2, so this is not a matter of interpretation. Live, through the engine's own exitInterior() and buildingAt(), 39 of 40 doors tested leave the player inside the building they just left, 35 of them by more than a metre of clearance. Round 4's roof fix, which is correct, closes the lid.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: RI-WLD13 is interior/exterior continuity, and this is the other end of the same object the round just fixed. Four rounds have measured whether the building is big enough to contain its room; none has measured where you are standing when you come out of it. A player meets it by walking out of a door.
remedy: Re-derive buildings[].door as a point ON the entry wall: b.{x,z} offset by half the drawn depth along entrySideLocal(b), which render/exterior.js already computes in order to cut the doorway.

Re-derive continuity.exterior_spawn as a point ~1.5 m OUTSIDE that wall point, clamped out of every neighbouring footprint - the same clamp applyInteriorBounds() already applies to continuity.interior_spawn, pointed the other way.

Add the assertion to tools/check-building-fits-room.mjs, which already exists and already has a --self-break: no exterior_spawn may satisfy insideBuilding(plan, x, z, 0). Prove it goes red by moving one spawn inward.
biggest_gap.acceptance: insideBuilding() returns null for all 112 declared exterior_spawn points; a live sweep of all 115 doors reports 0 doorsteps inside a drawn footprint after exitInterior(); and the new check exits 1 when a single spawn is perturbed inward.

other_gaps.what: 55 authored lamps in 19 of the 41 shrunk rooms stand outside their own room's walls, 12 of them non-snuffable hearths, worst 2.33 m out - and 0 in any room the join did not shrink, so the join caused every one. render/interior.js sets each fitting and each PointLight at L.pos verbatim, and sim/stealth/system.js#syncInteriorLights() adds a detection light source at the identical verbatim pos inside the fixed step.
other_gaps.why_it_matters: The round says it states the cost of the fix plainly and this part of the cost is not stated at all. A hearth is snuffable:false - the one light a player cannot put out - and twelve of them are now on the wrong side of a wall, feeding the Souls-side detection curve from outside the room.
remedy: Clamp lights[] in applyInteriorBounds() exactly as continuity.interior_spawn is already clamped, stashing a lights_declared copy so the pass stays idempotent and reversible.
other_gaps.acceptance: 0 authored lamps outside their room's bounds_m on 115 of 115, measured by tools/world/critic-w1-04-r4-offline.mjs C3, and lightSourceCensus() agreeing with the drawn fittings.

other_gaps.what: w1-04-consumption.mjs section 10a takes sigStreet BEFORE opening the door - which is wherever the previous door's exit left the body - and requires sigBack === sigStreet after leaving THIS door. Across a town boundary it compares Helstrom's street with Archon's and calls the difference a failure to restore the exterior. That is the whole of the 105-of-115 shortfall: 4 of 4 failures in my 32-door replication are settlement changes, all with room_was_drawn true and room_differs_from_street true.
other_gaps.why_it_matters: The aggregation is red on a green build, and the builder has never seen its output. The vacuous check it replaced was condemned by the round-3 critic; its replacement is a fact about the probe on 10 of 115 doors.
remedy: Read the street at the door being tested rather than at the previous one: exit, step, then take sigStreet - or take it after enterInterior() has established which town the door is in.
other_gaps.acceptance: w1-04-consumption.mjs exits 0 with exterior_restored_on_exit == entered == 115, and the cut arm still reads 0.

other_gaps.what: There is no paving, yard, market stall or ground-material change of any kind between a town and the terrain it stands on, in any of the eight settlements. Unchanged since round 1 and visible in every picture in this verdict.
other_gaps.why_it_matters: With roofs now closing every building, this is the largest remaining visual gap in RI-WLD03 and the reason a town still reads as buildings standing in a field.
remedy: A ground-material pass keyed off settlement radius and the building footprints, drawn by province.js alongside the buildings it already draws.
other_gaps.acceptance: Every settlement draws a distinguishable ground surface inside its radius, measurable as a material/mesh census in tools/world/w1-04-r3-exterior.mjs.

corpus_extended.what: A geometry signature that survives a null control, and the eleven degenerate cases it must pass before it may report a cross-subject number. The direct answer to GAP-W1-pixel-acceptance-is-unmeasurable from the round-3 verdict.

Two scope limits of that signature, written down before someone builds on it: it counts meshes that are visible:false (Object3D.traverse visits invisible children), and it is blind to lighting and to every material property except colour. Both are conservative for a distinctness claim and both would make a teardown that HIDES rather than REMOVES an inert control.

A fourth shape for RULES.md rule 6's taxonomy: a check that is neither inert nor vacuous but MIS-SPECIFIED - it fails on a green build because its two arms are read at different places. Distinguishable from the other three only by attributing failures row by row.

gap_closure.note: Closed and verified independently rather than taken. Reproduced in bare Node off the shipped planSettlement() and applyInteriorBounds(): 41 of 112 before, 0 after, worst area ratio 1.0887, 41 rooms limited by the plan, worst archon-market keeping 0.1714. The 2x2 delete-the-fix is honestly labelled as two-guards-for-one-defect and I reproduced its two corner cells. The COST is understated: 55 lamps and 292 meshes are now outside the rooms they belong to.

The pixel sweep now measures its own noise floor first and refuses to report a cross-room number, and the replacement - getDrawnSignature() - passes eleven degenerate cases including the one the pixel hash fails outright: one unchanged room read at 0, 2, 60 and 600 fixed steps returns ONE hash where the pixel hash returned 8 of 8 distinct after 2 steps.

__w1_04_perturbSettlement no longer nulls engine._townCell behind _settleSettlementSolids()'s back; it clears _townSolids and calls the method that owns the handle, with the voided measurement named in the comment.

The vacuous check is gone and its replacement genuinely reads the scene and genuinely goes red in the cut arm (0 vs 115). But the replacement is mis-specified across town boundaries and returns 105 of 115 on a green build, which is why the aggregation exits 1.

self_audit.self_audit_note: NOT DONE, plainly: the uncapped 115-room LIVE distinctness sweep (L3) - I replicated 32 doors live for the L1 attribution and 40 for L6, and the 115 remains offline-only, so the dispatch's question about whether an offline count is evidence about what a player sees is answered for 40 doors and not for 115; RI-WLD03 M13 (rule 25 binds me too, and I took the top-down shot it needs); inCoverFraction on both arms; the observed-theft branch. THREE PROBE DEFECTS OF MY OWN are reported in the verdict rather than buried: (1) my first offline census called buildInterior(rec) instead of buildInterior(root, rec), traversed 0 meshes in 115 of 115 rooms and reported a clean 'nothing outside the room' - rule 4 caught it and the fixed run gives the opposite answer, 292 meshes outside in 63 rooms; (2) I read whereAmI().door instead of .door_in_reach and briefly had 'you cannot get back in', which I do not claim; (3) my 'people in the room' arm recorded npcs_in_sim: 0 and proves nothing about moving bodies. METHOD DEVIATION: I killed my own stalled live run with an unscoped pkill -f headless_shell, which may have taken a neighbour's browser with it; reported under rule 26.
